experiment: Actual local Claude CLI planning followed by shared Hydra-assisted execution
limitations: One sample per case/arm; no statistical generalization claimed.
Failure counts remain in the attempt denominator; scored report rates are explicitly conditional.
Every arm shares Hydra-assisted safety/recursive refresh; blocking is not a baseline safety comparison.
Provider costs are reported list estimates, not a claim about subscription billing.
Exact flat traversal can tie graph correctness; this does not prove a unique database advantage.

protocol.arm_order: fixed rotation by case index; all plans frozen before any refresh
protocol.blocking_interpretation: Missing-source blocking comes from the shared executor and does not establish a planning advantage.
protocol.executor: Every arm uses the same Hydra-assisted currentness and recursive refresh executor.
protocol.primary_metric: fresh affected reports after actual tool refresh; per-case outcomes retained
protocol.scope: Small authored retrieval/planning pilot. Report composition is predefined, not invented by the model.
protocol.token_accounting: Retrieval budget counts canonical JSONL without file terminator. Provider usage includes CLI/schema/system/cache overhead; cl100k estimates are separate.
